svg.text: The Sixfold front end: choosing the next PC every cycle, before any instruction is decoded
Performance build (src/Riscv64.sv). FETCH1 guesses with the Branch Target Buffer and a tournament of two direction predictors; FETCH2 corrects cheap cases; EXECUTE checks and trains.
look up 4 tables in parallel with the instruction cache
16 entries, direct mapped: "the instruction at this PC jumped to that PC"
two predictors answer "taken?"; a third table picks which one to trust
learns each branch on its own
the last 6 branch directions: FETCH2 shifts in
each guess, EXECUTE repairs it after a flush
counter >= 2: trust gshare, else the BHT;
moves toward whichever one was right
and FETCH1 did not already jump:
training writes: one per resolved branch, at the table indexes saved when it was predicted
Every table entry is a 2-bit saturating counter
Predict taken when the counter is 2 or 3. One odd outcome only moves it one step, so a loop
branch that falls through once at the end is not unlearned. Reset value: 10 (weakly taken).
Cost: 128 + 64 + 128 counters = 640 bits of direction state, plus a 16-entry BTB.
What each case costs (bubbles = lost cycles)
not a branch, or not taken and predicted so
taken branch / JAL already in the BTB
taken branch / JAL not in the BTB yet (FETCH2)
axis starts at 50% (a coin flip). TAGE is the basis of current Intel, AMD and Arm predictors.
